THA in its own hand. The signature voice admitted by **UIA §8 (amended by UXHOME1)**, which replaced *"two voices only; no third typeface, ever"* with three named families and a hard boundary: the signature is for **emotionally significant branded moments only** and is forbidden in all functional UI — buttons, forms, navigation, tables, cards, modals, planner, shopping. `.text-signature` is the ONE entry point: no `font-signature` Tailwind utility exists, deliberately (tailwind.config.ts carries the comment saying so), because a utility would be a one-token door into the third typeface from any surface in the product. **The webfont is not loaded in production** — the token resolves, but the only surface that fetches Caveat is the dev-only prototype below, so no household downloads a font for a page they cannot reach. **Permitted surfaces — exactly three, and none is a household surface:** `pages/dev/arrival-experience.tsx` (`/dev/arrival`, ARRIVAL1), `pages/dev/arrival-a-welcome.tsx` (`/dev/arrival-a-welcome`, EXP2 exploration Prototype A — admitted by a governed edit, 2026-07-15, for the same emotionally significant moment: the arrival greeting, and nothing else), and `pages/dev/arrival-s1-quiet.tsx` (`/dev/arrival-s1-quiet`, EXP3 synthesis candidate S1 — admitted by this governed edit, 2026-07-15, carrying Prototype A's greeting forward into the synthesis: the same one moment, the arrival greeting, and nothing else). All three are `import.meta.env.DEV` only; the chunks are dropped from the production bundle, verified in the build. This surface replaced UXHOME1's `home-arrival-prototype.tsx`, which was discarded by ARRIVAL1 — the signature voice now says its one word ("Welcome home") inside an *arrival* rather than over an animated Home page. A second surface does not follow from the first: §8 requires a further governed decision, per surface. The failure mode this row exists to catch is not ugliness but **familiarity** — the moment the signature becomes an ordinary UI font, the identity it was admitted to carry is gone and using it more cannot bring it back.

UXHOME1 amended the law and built the prototype and deliberately did NOT adopt it into the live Home in the same change; adoption was a separate, explicit decision. **That decision is now recorded: ADOPT (Colin Clapson, 2026-07-17, via ODL2)** — see the open migration. This exemption stands only until the North Star Home workstream executes it, and then it goes, replaced by exactly one named permitted surface.

This row was recorded on the day the prototype was built rather than after it was forgotten, because a prototype nobody decided about is how a third typeface enters a product by accident — the exact failure the original § 8 rule was written to prevent, and the one the amendment is only safe against if this row is honoured. **The row is not discharged by the decision.** ADOPT recorded and unexecuted is still an authored-but-unadopted successor sitting live-looking in the tree (PX1's PageHeader.tsx, exactly). It closes when the prototypes are deleted, not when the decision is minuted. ODL2 recorded the ruling and did not execute it, because execution edits Home and ODL2 was governance only.
openMigration.remaining: **The execution of ADOPT**, in one change, owned by the North Star Home workstream: fold the Arrival Experience greeting into home-experience-page.tsx; move the Caveat `@import` into client/src/index.css so the webfont is loaded in production for the first time; name `/home` as the ONE permitted surface in this row; and DELETE every exploration prototype — `/dev/arrival` (ARRIVAL1), the five EXP2 prototypes (`/dev/arrival-{a..e}-*`) and the two EXP3 synthesis candidates (`/dev/arrival-s1-quiet`, `/dev/arrival-s2-walking-home`) — with their routes. ODL1 built Home's greeting in the **display** voice as the lawful interim, so the upgrade is a one-line change to that greeting plus the deletions. **Three constraints ride on the execution.** (1) § 8's "a second surface does not follow from the first": `/home` is one surface, and Home's greeting is one moment — not Home's headings, labels or values. (2) Blueprint § 12.2 caps the Living Detail at **at most once per day**, and § 10 there holds the signature "arrival-only". (3) The webfont becomes a production download for the first time; it is a household's bandwidth, so it is subject to UIA § 15's floors and must not block the greeting's paint. **What may not happen is the third outcome**: the prototypes surviving their own decision. ADOPT was chosen; the deletions are not optional, and they are what closes this row.

concerns.concern: Depth, warm light and materiality (the § 4 vocabulary)
concerns.owner: index.css (the ground, light, warm-shadow, penumbra and radius tokens)
concerns.owns: **The § 4 depth and light vocabulary, as values** — the ground plane (materiality), warm shadow (depth), one light and the penumbra (warm light), plus the radius ladder that governs what rests on what. **The law is UIA § 4** (amended by ODL2); this file is the values' one home (§ 16). One row, not three: EXP4's central finding is that *"depth is believable exactly when it describes ONE room — one ground, one light, one direction, every shadow explaining a distance"*, so three owners could drift from one another, which is the exact failure the vocabulary forbids. **The values graduated from EXP4 Study A (The Warm Layered Workspace), selected by ODL2 on 2026-07-17 — and selected on LAW, not on taste.** Studies B and C set type directly on the orchard (their headings, reminders and list rows sit on the landscape in their own screenshots), and Blueprint § 6.1 gives type ground beneath it *"without negotiation"*; § 4 now says the same. EXP4 itself judged C *"one step too little — support needs an anchor"*. A was the only study with a ground plane, which is the vocabulary's central member. **B and C were DELETED in the same change** (§ 17, retire on introduction), with their routes and their capture-harness entries. **Dark mode is completely resolved** (§ 16 forbids a partial mode): every warm shadow resolves to `none` rather than to a dimmer warm shadow, because the vocabulary IS a morning sun and at night there is no sun — a warm shadow at midnight is a lie about where the light comes from, and § 4 admits depth only to describe space truthfully. Rank is carried at night by tint and border: the same hierarchy, a different instrument. Study A had independently reached that answer. This closes Blueprint § 18 open item 4 for this vocabulary. **The ambient light pool declares a ceiling, not a pairing** (`--light-ambient-ceiling`), per the § 15 rule ODL2 added: a graded surface carrying no text has no colour pairing to measure, so it names the strength it may never exceed instead — which is what EXP4 asked for when it flagged its own radial pool as needing *"a named token with a stated ceiling"*.

openMigration.finding: ODL2 (2026-07-17) — the vocabulary is admitted, valued and consumed, but its only consumer is a development-only reference.
openMigration.owner: Colin Clapson — with the North Star Home implementation, the first household surface that needs a ground
openMigration.remaining: **Home's E3, and then a deletion.** `pages/dev/material-a-warm-layers.tsx` (`/dev/material-a-warm-layers`) is the vocabulary's **reference implementation** and its sole consumer: it holds these tokens honest, and it is the surface that proves them by being looked at. It is `import.meta.env.DEV` only, so no household downloads it. **Its deletion trigger is Home's adoption of the ground plane** — when Home stands at E3 on a real ground, this page and `scripts/capture-exp4-materiality-depth.ts` are deleted in that same change, completing the disposition EXP4 § 6 set for all three studies. **Why it was not deleted with B and C**: EXP4 § 6 assumed the ideas would graduate into a *language*, and they graduated into *tokens* — which need a consumer. Deleting A would have left twenty-one tokens defined and adopted by nothing: the authored-but-unadopted foundation this register exists to make impossible, and the precise state UIA § 17 says it exists to end. Keeping the winner as the reference until the real surface lands is the same shape this register already blesses for `signature-typography`, and it is recorded here with its trigger so it cannot outlive its purpose quietly.
openMigration.why: The vocabulary is real, valued and visible, and it is still adopted by nothing a household can reach — so it is recorded, not assumed. This row closes when Home consumes the tokens and the reference dies; it does not close when the values look right. **E2's exposure value and this vocabulary's dark resolution are the two things no surface can yet verify**: no E2 room exists, and THA's dark theme is unreachable (see `theme-colour-mode`). Both are reasoned decisions with their reasoning written down, sitting in one place, cheap to correct on the day something can finally show them wrong.

orphans.note: A module under these roots with **zero importers** is authored-but-unadopted — the failure state UIA §17 exists to end, and the mechanism behind PX1's `PageHeader.tsx` (a full unadopted successor to `WorkspaceHeader`, sitting live-looking in the tree for a future workstream to adopt *instead of* the real owner). PX1-W4.7 deleted 26 such files. These are what the gate found **after** that sweep — none of them known to any PX1 workstream, all of them found by the register on the day it was built.
